answer: Divergent history proof. Each agent must wander through a random challenge sequence seeded per epoch, and the network records a short hash of its path. Clones share identical histories, so they cannot answer divergent follow-ups; honest agents diverge freely. An attacker must run each clone through a distinct path to reach the zenith of valid responses, paying full compute per identity. Shale-like cheap clones fail the divergence check, forcing per-identity replication cost.
